name: Levetiracetam
meta: 250 mg, 500 mg, 750 mg, 1000 mg tablets; 100 mg/mL oral solution
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder, very soluble in water.

Discovered during evaluation of piracetam analogues; the S-enantiomer of etiracetam showed potent anti-seizure effects in audiogenic and kindling models. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1999 (UCB Pharma).
250 mg, 500 mg, 750 mg, 1000 mg tablets; 100 mg/mL oral solution

Binds synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, modulating neurotransmitter release; also inhibits N-type calcium channels and opposes negative modulators of GABA/glycine currents. Receptor / target profile: Binds synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) and inhibits presynaptic N-type calcium channels, reducing neurotransmitter release.
Enzymatic hydrolysis of the acetamide group (not CYP-dependent)
Summary: Rapid, near-complete absorption (~100%); Tmax ~1 h. <10% protein bound. Not CYP-metabolised (enzymatic hydrolysis). Half-life ~7 h. Renally excreted – adjust dose to creatinine clearance.
Partial-onset seizures with or without secondary generalisation (monotherapy ≥16 years; adjunct ≥1 month)
Myoclonic seizures in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (adjunct, ≥12 years)
Adults: 500 mg twice daily; increase by 500 mg twice daily every 2–4 weeks; max 1500 mg twice daily
Children (≥6 months, <50 kg): 10 mg/kg twice daily, up to 30 mg/kg twice daily
Renal impairment: CrCl 50–79 – 500–1000 mg BD; 30–49 – 250–750 mg BD; <30 – 250–500 mg BD
With or without food; withdraw gradually
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl 50–79: 500–1000 mg BD; 30–49: 250–750 mg BD; <30: 250–500 mg BD; ESRD on dialysis: 500–1000 mg OD + 250–500 mg after dialysis.
No adjustment except severe impairment with renal impairment (reduce 50%).
Relatively favourable among antiepileptics; levels fall in pregnancy – monitor.
Excreted in milk; breastfeeding possible with monitoring.
Hypersensitivity to levetiracetam or pyrrolidone derivatives
Behavioural changes – irritability, aggression, depression, psychosis
Mood and behaviour; renal function; CBC if infections.
Somnolence, agitation, aggression, respiratory depression, coma. Supportive care; haemodialysis removes ~50%.
SANAD II (Lancet 2021) – lamotrigine preferred to levetiracetam for focal epilepsy; valproate superior for generalised epilepsy.
ESETT (Kapur et al., NEJM 2019) – IV levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate similarly effective in benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus.
Oral solution – use the measuring syringe provided
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
